subject: ss-haematology
title: Acquired coagulopathies DIC mixing study traps and liver disease
refs: Harrison Principles of Internal Medicine 22e Ch 121 Coagulation Disorders
BSH guideline on acquired haemophilia A 2023

steps.tx: Clotting times sort acquired bleeding fast. **PT** (prothrombin time) tests the **extrinsic pathway** (tissue factor route) and falls first in vitamin K deficiency. **aPTT** (activated partial thromboplastin time) tests the **intrinsic pathway** (contact route) and prolongs in inhibitors and haemophilia. **Thrombin time** (TT, final step test) prolongs in low **fibrinogen** (clotting protein) and sample contamination. **Both prolonged** with low fibrinogen shouts **DIC** (consumption coagulopathy).
steps.say: PT tests the extrinsic pathway and falls first in vitamin K deficiency. aPTT tests the intrinsic pathway and prolongs in inhibitors. Both prolonged with low fibrinogen shouts DIC.

steps.tx: **DIC** (disseminated intravascular coagulation) consumes factors and platelets together. **Sepsis** (infection), **malignancy** (cancer), **obstetric catastrophe** (amniotic embolism) and **trauma** (crush injury) drive it. **Schistocytes** (sheared red cells) appear with **thrombocytopenia** (low platelets). **Fibrinogen** (clotting protein) falls and **D dimer** (fibrin breakdown marker) soars. **ISTH score** (International Society scoring system) at or above **five** defines overt DIC.
steps.say: DIC consumes clotting factors and platelets together. Sepsis malignancy and obstetric catastrophe cause most DIC. An ISTH score above five is the definition of overt DIC.

steps.tx: **ISTH DIC score** (scoring system) adds four items: platelets, D dimer, PT prolongation and fibrinogen. A score **above five** means overt DIC and daily repetition is advised. A score **below five** suggests nonovert DIC and repeat testing in **one** to **two** days. **Pregnancy DIC** needs a separate scoring tool because fibrinogen runs higher in pregnancy. **Chronic DIC** (Trousseau syndrome in cancer) runs low grade with raised D dimer and near normal platelets.
steps.say: The ISTH score is made of platelets D dimer PT and fibrinogen. A score above five is overt DIC clearly. Pregnancy DIC needs a separate scoring tool.

nodes.label: Below five: repeat one to two days

steps.tx: Treating DIC means treating its driver first. **Underlying cause control** (antibiotics for sepsis, delivery, chemotherapy) stops consumption. **Platelets** (blood cells) are transfused below **fifty thousand** per microlitre with bleeding or before surgery. **Fibrinogen concentrate** (protein replacement) or cryoprecipitate (frozen plasma fraction) corrects fibrinogen below **one point five** grams per litre. **Fresh frozen plasma** (FFP, frozen plasma) covers multiple factor losses in bleeding patients. **Blood thinners** have no routine DIC role.
steps.say: Treating DIC means controlling the underlying cause first. Platelets are transfused below fifty thousand with bleeding. Fibrinogen concentrate corrects fibrinogen below one point five grams.

steps.tx: **Mixing study** (correction test) separates deficiency from inhibitor. A **one to one mix** (equal patient plus normal plasma) corrects **factor deficiency** immediately. **Inhibitors** (antibodies) fail immediate correction or correct then prolong again at **thirty seven** degrees after **one** to **two** hours. **Acquired haemophilia A** (anti factor VIII autoimmunity) shows time dependent non correction. **Bethesda assay** (inhibitor quantification test) measures strength in Bethesda units.
steps.say: Mixing studies separate factor deficiency from inhibitors. Deficiency is corrected immediately in the mix. Acquired haemophilia A is corrected then prolongs at thirty seven degrees here.

steps.tx: **Acquired haemophilia A** (autoimmune factor VIII loss) strikes older adults, often after childbirth. Bleeding pattern is severe: skin, muscle and mucosal bleeds dominate. **Joint bleeds** (haemarthroses), the hallmark of inherited disease, stay rare here. **Factor VIII activity** (clotting level) can be near normal while inhibitor titres run high. **Steroids** plus **B cell antibody therapy** eradicate the autoantibody in most patients.
steps.say: Acquired haemophilia A affects older adults after childbirth often. Joint bleeds are rare in acquired disease. Steroids with antibody therapy are used to eradicate the autoantibody.

steps.tx: **Liver disease coagulopathy** (clotting failure in liver failure) is balanced, not purely prohaemorrhagic. The liver makes factors **II V VII IX X** (clotting proteins) and **protein C S** (regulators) alike. **INR** (international normalised ratio) therefore overreads bleeding risk in cirrhosis. **Thrombosis** (clots) still strikes cirrhotic patients, including portal vein thrombosis. **Thromboelastography** (whole blood clot test) guides products better than INR alone.
steps.say: Both clotting factors and regulators are low in liver disease. INR is not a reliable bleeding guide in cirrhosis. Thromboelastography guides products better than INR alone today.

steps.tx: **Vitamin K deficiency** (nutrient clotting defect) prolongs PT before aPTT moves. **Vitamin K antagonist** effect mimics dietary deficiency exactly. **PIVKA II** (proteins induced by vitamin K absence) levels rise in deficiency states. **Vitamin K trial** (slow intravenous dose) corrects deficiency within **twelve** to **twenty four** hours. **Cholestasis** (bile flow block) causes malabsorption of fat soluble vitamin K in chronic disease.
steps.say: Vitamin K deficiency is seen in prolonged PT before aPTT moves. A vitamin K trial is a test for deficiency within twelve to twenty four hours. Cholestasis causes vitamin K malabsorption in chronic disease.

nodes.label: Corrects in twelve to twenty four hours

steps.tx: **Acquired von Willebrand disease** (autoimmune vessel factor loss) follows **MGUS** (silent clone), lymphomas and myeloproliferative disease. **Ristocetin cofactor** (activity assay) falls with normal platelet counts. **Hormone treatment** gives brief correction in mild cases. **Acquired hemophilia** (autoimmune factor loss) shows the mixing study non correction pattern already discussed. **Sample contamination** (blood sample error) prolongs thrombin time and corrects with enzyme treatment.
steps.say: Acquired von Willebrand disease follows MGUS and lymphomas. Ristocetin cofactor falls with normal platelet counts in patients. Sample contamination is a cause of prolonged thrombin time in samples today.

steps.tx: Exam stems trap the following. **DIC** (consumption) lowers fibrinogen, while **TMA** (vessel clot) preserves it. **Mixing study** correction means deficiency, while non correction means inhibitor. **Vitamin K** (antidote vitamin) corrects deficiency but never inhibitor disease. **ISTH score five** is the overt DIC cutoff examiners demand by number.
steps.say: DIC is marked by low fibrinogen while TMA preserves it. Mixing study correction means deficiency and non correction means inhibitor. ISTH score five is the overt DIC cutoff.

steps.tx: High-yield for the exam: **DIC** is driven by **sepsis** and **malignancy**, scored by **ISTH at five** for overt disease. **Mixing study** corrects in deficiency and fails in inhibitors. **Acquired haemophilia A** spares joints and is treated with **steroids antibody therapy**. **Vitamin K** corrects deficiency in **twelve to twenty four** hours, and **liver INR** overreads bleeding risk.
steps.say: DIC scores above five are overt disease. Mixing studies correct in deficiency and fail in inhibitors. Vitamin K is a trial correcting deficiency within twelve to twenty four hours.
